title: Young Children Injured through Accidental Burns
what_it_is: Young Children Injured through Accidental Burns

sections.label: Child burn injuries and prevention
sections.summary: MOH monitors child burn cases via the National Trauma Registry, and prevention information is in the HPB Child Health Booklet and hospital programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) monitors the number of young children with burn injuries through the National Trauma Registry.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The incidence of notified cases of burns in children below the age of 16 years between 2011 and 2015, averaged 70 cases per 100,000 population.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This adds to 580 cases per year, on average.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Approximately half of the cases occurred among children under three years old and more than three-quarters of the cases occurred at home.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Of the cases occurring at home, half happened in the kitchens.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Information on burns prevention are included in the child safety checklist in the Health Promotion Board (HPB)'s Child Health Booklet, which is issued to every child born in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Hospitals also conduct community education programmes to raise awareness of burns and scalds, which include talks to childcare teachers on child safety, information pamphlets to parents, as well as educational videos which are hosted on their websites and played at hospital clinics.

sections.label: Child safety checklist contents
sections.summary: The Health Booklets Children Safety Checklist gives guidelines and advice on bath water, hot drinks and electrical outlets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The materials are very comprehensive in the Health Booklets Children Safety Checklist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: It provides guidelines and it also includes advice on preparing water for child's bath, as well as ensuring that hot drinks are out of reach of children, and ensuring that electrical outlets are not within children's reach.
